blocks.text: 1. System Prompting

blocks.alt: A system prompt shapes model behavior

blocks.text: System Prompting, opening the Prompt Engineering for RAG module by defining the model's overall role and behavior, shifts focus from context assembly to instruction writing.
It writes persistent instructions that shape how the model behaves across every single query.
2. Context Management Recap
Seven topics covered assembling the finished prompt from selected, prepared context.
Prompt engineering covers how the instructions within that prompt actually get written.

blocks.text: 3. What A System Prompt Actually Controls

blocks.alt: A system prompt controls tone, format, and grounding rules

blocks.text: The system prompt occupies the fixed instructions section of every request.
Defining tone, role, and behavioral boundaries that apply to every single query.
4. Grounding The Response In Retrieved Context

blocks.alt: A system prompt instructs use only provided context

blocks.text: As with separating instructions from retrieved content in Prompt Construction, a RAG system prompt instructs the model to answer using only the provided context.
Explicitly discouraging the model from relying on its own unrelated background knowledge instead.
5. Handling Missing Information Explicitly

blocks.alt: No answer in context is instructed to say I do not know

blocks.text: A well written system prompt tells the model exactly what to do when the retrieved context does not contain an answer.
Preventing the model from confidently guessing when it actually has no relevant information.

blocks.title: Note
blocks.content: An instruction like "if the context does not contain the answer, say so explicitly,", prevents a model from confidently fabricating a plausible sounding but incorrect answer when its retrieved context is insufficient.

blocks.text: 6. Defining Tone And Format

blocks.alt: A system prompt sets tone and format rules

blocks.text: The system prompt can specify whether responses should be concise, formal, or structured in a particular way.
Keeping that presentation consistent across every single response the model produces.
7. Persistent Versus Per-Query Instructions

blocks.alt: Persistent system prompt instructions are compared against per-query user message instructions

blocks.text: As with placing the query itself in Prompt Construction, the system prompt stays fixed while the user query changes every request.
That persistence is exactly what makes it the right place for stable, reusable rules.

blocks.title: Note
blocks.content: Rules that apply to every query, like always citing sources or always staying within the provided context, belong in the persistent system prompt rather than being repeated in every individual user query.

blocks.text: 8. Keeping System Prompts Focused
As with final token validation in Prompt Construction, an overly long system prompt consumes token budget on every single request.
A focused, concise system prompt leaves more room for the actual retrieved content.

blocks.content: {"headers":["System prompt style","Effect on available budget"],"rows":[["Long, exhaustive instructions","Consumes token budget on every single request"],["Focused, concise instructions","Leaves more room for retrieved content"]]}

blocks.text: 9. Recognizing What Belongs In A System Prompt

blocks.alt: Something stable across all queries points toward the system prompt

blocks.text: Stable rules like grounding, tone, and missing information handling belong in the system prompt.
The actual user question or retrieved chunks belong in the per-query sections instead in Prompt Construction.
10. Worked Example
The example below directly demonstrates writing a focused system prompt with grounding and missing information rules.

code.content:
system_prompt = """You are a support assistant. Follow these rules:
1. Answer only using the provided context below.
2. If the context does not contain the answer, say "I don't have enough information to answer that."
3. Keep responses concise and cite the source of each fact using [source: X].
4. Do not use outside knowledge beyond what is provided."""

def build_full_prompt(system_prompt, context_section, user_query):
    # what a system prompt actually controls
    return f"{system_prompt}\n\n### Context\n{context_section}\n\n### Question\n{user_query}"

context_section = "[source: handbook_v3] Refunds are processed within five business days."
user_query = "How long does a refund take?"

full_prompt = build_full_prompt(system_prompt, context_section, user_query)
print("Full assembled prompt:\n")
print(full_prompt)

print(f"\nSystem prompt length (keeping system prompts focused): {len(system_prompt.split())} words")

blocks.title: Note
blocks.content: Running this example shows the system prompt establishing grounding, missing information handling, and citation rules once, applying consistently regardless of what specific question or context follows it, exactly the persistent versus per-query instructions distinction.

blocks.text: 11. Common Mistakes

items: Writing a system prompt so long that it consumes a large share of every request's token budget.
Forgetting to instruct the model on what to do when retrieved context lacks an answer.
Repeating stable, reusable rules in every user query instead of placing them in the system prompt.
Omitting explicit grounding instructions, letting the model rely on unrelated background knowledge.

blocks.text: 12. Key Takeaways

items: System prompting writes persistent instructions that shape model behavior across every query.
It occupies the fixed instructions section, defining role, tone, and behavioral boundaries.
A RAG system prompt should instruct the model to answer using only the provided context.
A well written prompt tells the model what to do when the context lacks an answer.
The system prompt can specify consistent tone and format across every response.
It stays fixed across every query, making it the right place for stable, reusable rules.
An overly long system prompt consumes token budget better spent on retrieved content.
Stable rules belong in the system prompt; the specific question belongs in the per-query section.
